data.name: Manesh
data.gender_notes: Manesh is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Manesh is a Sanskrit name derived from the word 'manas' meaning mind and 'isha' meaning god or ruler. It is believed to be the name of the moon god in Hindu mythology. The name Manesh carries the meaning “Moon God” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Manesh usually hope their child will grow to embody moon god and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the divine presence of the moon god, bestowing wisdom, tranquility, and intuition.
data.etymology: Manesh belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Moon God.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Manesh total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

data.cultural_impact: Manesh holds great significance in Hindu culture, particularly in Maharashtra, India. It is an uncommon but beautiful name that reflects the deity of the moon. The name is also associated with the worship of the god Ganesha, who is believed to be the god of intelligence, wisdom, and new beginnings, and is often invoked before starting any new ventures. Manesh is also mentioned in Hindu epics like the Mahabharata and the Puranas.
data.spiritual_significance: Manesh carries a deep spiritual significance in Hinduism. As mentioned earlier, the name is derived from the words 'manas' and 'isha,' signifying the ruler or god of the mind. In Hinduism, it is believed that the mind is the source of all thoughts and actions, and controlling the mind is crucial for achieving spiritual growth and inner peace. Therefore, the name Manesh holds the power to remind us of the importance of mental focus and discipline in our spiritual journey towards enlightenment.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Manesh is a name derived from the Sanskrit word "Manas," which means mind or intellect. The name symbolizes the individual's deep connection with wisdom and understanding, encouraging them to seek knowledge and use their intellect to navigate through life's challenges.

historical_references.reference: Manesh was an important Jain Tirthankara. He is believed to have lived around the 8th century BC in the Aravalli hills region of Rajasthan, India.

Manesh is also mentioned in Hindu mythology as the king of the Nagas (serpents) and the lord of the mountain Meru. He is said to have protected the devas (gods) from the demon Vritra and is revered as a deity in some parts of India.
